extracted.intended_audience: federal agency policy/staff responsible for standards use and development, NIST/OMB staff, agency general counsels
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory policies for Federal agencies on adopting, using, participating in, and reporting about voluntary consensus technical standards and related conformity assessment activities under OMB Circular A-119 and P.L. 104-113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption in favor of voluntary consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy of the federal government is to rely on voluntary standards, both domestic and international, whenever feasible and consistent with law and regulation; reliance on voluntary consensus standards conserves agency resources and avoids imposing additional costs on the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This longstanding presumption applies to procurement and regulatory activities. Agencies should prefer voluntary consensus standards over government-unique standards except where inconsistent with law or otherwise impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory duty to use technical standards developed/adopted by voluntary consensus bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies and departments 'shall use technical standards that are developed or adopted by voluntary consensus standards bodies' and, in carrying out this requirement, 'shall consult with voluntary, private sector, consensus standards bodies and shall, when such participation is in the public interest and is compatible with agency and departmental missions, authorities, priorities, and budget resources, participate with such bodies in the development of technical standards.' (P.L. 104-113, §12(d)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consider and, where appropriate, adopt voluntary consensus technical standards; participation is mandated when consistent with mission/authority/priorities/resources and in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for inconsistent or impractical standards; mandatory explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may use standards other than voluntary consensus standards where use of the latter would be 'inconsistent with applicable law or otherwise impractical.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an agency elects to use non-voluntary (e.g., government-unique) standards for those reasons, the head of the agency must send to OMB, through NIST, an explanation of the reasons for using such standards. Beginning with FY1997, OMB will transmit an annual summary of these explanations to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting to NIST/OMB about standards activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to submit information about their voluntary consensus standards activities for each fiscal year to NIST (for OMB reporting). NIST prepares an annual report for OMB to transmit to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should include adoptions of voluntary consensus standards, substitutions of voluntary standards for government-unique standards, and explanations for any use of government-unique standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and attributes of 'voluntary consensus standard'
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary consensus standards are technical standards developed and used by private sector organizations (standards development organizations) that have characteristics of consensus (openness, balance of interests, due process, and absence of sustained opposition), and include provisions on availability of intellectual property on non-discriminatory, reasonable-royalty or royalty-free terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular clarifies consensus need not be unanimity ('but not necessarily unanimity') and retains emphasis on openness, balance, and due process. Agencies may determine whether a standards body qualifies by applying criteria in the Circular (final section 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of 'impractical' use of voluntary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular adopts a broad definition of 'impractical' (including terms such as infeasible, inadequate, inefficient) for purposes of allowing use of non-voluntary standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide an explanation of the reasons why a voluntary standard is impractical. OMB decided not to require agencies to describe remedial steps to overcome the impracticality (that would be unduly burdensome). The Circular deleted 'demonstrably' to avoid implying a greater level of proof than required by the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to consult and participate in standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consult with voluntary consensus standards bodies and participate in standards development when such participation is in the public interest and compatible with agency missions, authorities, priorities, and budget resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation helps ensure creation of standards usable by agencies and leverages private-sector expertise. Agencies are encouraged to coordinate participation to make effective use of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit participation to mission-related activities; refrain otherwise
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency representatives must refrain from active participation in voluntary consensus standards bodies or their committees when participating does not relate to the mission of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 7 clarifies agencies should avoid participation for matters unrelated to their statutory mission and that such participation would be contrary to the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of dominance and appearance of impropriety
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should monitor participation to prevent dominating proceedings or creating the appearance of impropriety; employees must avoid the practice or appearance of undue influence in their representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular expects agencies to ensure their members do not dominate standards development and to work with private-sector oversight organizations (e.g., ANSI) to maintain fair, balanced consensus processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal contractors acting as agency representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal contractors are not included within the definition of 'agency'; however, if a federal contractor participates in a voluntary consensus standards body on behalf of an agency (as an agency representative or liaison), the contractor must comply with the Circular's participation policies (e.g., may not dominate proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts that involve contractor participation in standards work must ensure contractor behavior aligns with agency obligations under the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies as full and equal participants (not specially limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB decided not to impose specific limitations (such as prohibiting agency representatives from chairing or voting) because the Act and Circular promote full and equal federal participation in standards bodies when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While agencies are to be full participants, they remain responsible for ensuring participation is consistent with mission and does not result in undue influence or unfair processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on agency support for standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency support (funding, participation, etc.) for voluntary consensus standards bodies should be limited to that which clearly furthers agency and departmental missions, authorities, priorities, and budget resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support that does not clearly further agency missions risks being contrary to the Circular and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory incorporation requires proper regulatory analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when an agency determines a standard is a voluntary consensus standard, incorporation of that standard into regulation does not relieve the agency of performing the proper regulatory analysis (e.g., Principles of Regulation in Executive Order 12866).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should ensure that use of private-sector technical standards in regulations complies with regulatory review and analysis requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity assessment guidance led by NIST (Commerce)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular defers definition and detailed policy guidance on conformity assessment to NIST; OMB directs the Secretary of Commerce to issue policy guidance for conformity assessment activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow forthcoming NIST guidance on conformity assessment procedures and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of international standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are encouraged to rely on voluntary consensus standards 'both domestic and international' whenever feasible and consistent with law and regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular was revised to encourage consideration of international standards while clarifying applicability language to avoid unintended conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency determination of qualifying standards bodies; role of private accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of complying with the Circular, agencies may determine whether particular organizations qualify as voluntary consensus standards bodies by applying the operational criteria set out in the Circular (final section 4); accreditation/determination of specific organizations is primarily a private-sector function (e.g., ANSI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should apply the Circular's criteria (openness, balance, due process, etc.) when evaluating whether to treat standards from a body as 'voluntary consensus.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility on edition usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should not be strictly limited to considering only the latest edition of a voluntary consensus standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB modified the Circular to allow agencies discretion in edition selection where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public input mechanism for recommending standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised Circular establishes processes that enable interested members of the public to inform agencies of voluntary consensus standards that should be used in Federal procurements and regulations in lieu of government-unique standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should provide and follow processes for public submissions/recommendations about candidate voluntary standards for procurement and regulatory incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and limits of explanations for non-use
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency finds a voluntary consensus standard impractical or otherwise not used, the Act/Circular require an explanation of reasons; OMB decided not to require agencies to describe the steps necessary to overcome impracticality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations should be adequate to demonstrate why the voluntary standard was not adopted, but need not include burdensome 'remedy' plans beyond the statutory explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest guidance for federal employees serving on standards boards
rubrics_metrics.description: OGE/OLC concluded that Section 12 of the Act can authorize federal employees to serve as officers or directors of standards organizations in their official capacities to the extent those boards are engaged in standard-setting activities; if a board has only administrative responsibilities, §208 may bar such service absent a waiver or release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When service by an employee on a board is integral to statutory standard-setting participation, it may be permissible; agencies should consult OGE/OLC guidance and consider fiduciary duty and §208 implications. Administrative-only board service remains subject to conflict-of-interest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service in chair/subcommittee roles that impose no fiduciary duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Service as chair of a working committee or subcommittee, to the extent the position imposes no fiduciary duty and creates no employer-employee relationship, does not itself trigger 18 U.S.C. §208 disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies can permit employee chairs of working groups/subcommittees when those functions are part of the standards-setting role and do not create prohibited fiduciary interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of 'standard' and 'technical standard' terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular reorganized and clarified definitions, equating 'standard' with 'technical standard' for purposes of the policy, and distinguishing technical standards (products and processes) from 'regulatory standards' that set overall regulatory goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act/Circular apply to technical standards (size, strength, technical performance of products/processes) that may be referenced in regulations, but not to higher-level regulatory standards that set outcomes.
